hypotheses.statement: If a ClayCode FFI capability designates only a reusable host slot/resource number, drop+reuse can retarget an old capability/handle to a different live resource.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The runtime never reuses identities or independently version-checks every lookup, so slot-like values remain globally unique within the relevant lifetime.
hypotheses.falsifier: A concrete slot-reusing lowerer that preserves stale-handle rejection without any equivalent lifetime/version identity.

hypotheses.statement: FFI resources that can be lent temporarily need a machine-checkable lifetime/ownership distinction or an equivalent runtime mechanism; otherwise a borrow can escape the call boundary.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The ABI never exposes borrowed resources or the host language/runtime statically proves non-escape before lowering.
hypotheses.falsifier: A supported host ABI with temporary borrows that passes borrow-escape adversarial tests without an explicit or equivalent lifetime mechanism.
evidence: WebAssembly Component Model WIT resource own/borrow semantics

hypotheses.statement: The abstract ClayCode requirement should be lifetime-bound typed resource identity, not a prematurely fixed representation of {instance,slot,generation,mode}.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The explicit five-field representation is sufficiently portable and should be canonicalized now.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production lowerings across at least two host backends show the explicit representation is both necessary and lower-cost than alternative opaque globally-unique handles while preserving replay and authority invariants.
